title: ADH1B/ALDH2 alcohol-metabolism variants: biochemical-pathway positive control with population scope
summary: Positive-control record for MKH-PAT-0015. It calibrates candidate-gene failure narratives by preserving alcohol-metabolism variants as a case where biologically interpretable enzyme genes have strong, replicated associations while still requiring ancestry/population and health-outcome caution.

status_history.note: Promoted after rev0018 identified alcohol-metabolism variants as a candidate control for MKH-PAT-0015.

place.scope: alcohol flushing and alcohol-use/alcohol-dependence genetics; East Asian flushing GWAS scope especially explicit

claims.claim: Cho et al. report a GWAS meta-analysis and heritability analysis of alcohol flushing in 15,105 East-Asian-ancestry males and conclude that ALDH2-rs671 and ADH1B-rs1229984 are associated with alcohol flushing in East Asian populations.
what_would_change_status: A corrected article or later high-quality meta-analysis materially changes the association or sample-scope statement.

claims.claim: The same article explains the mechanistic pathway: ADH1B metabolizes alcohol into acetaldehyde, ALDH2 metabolizes acetaldehyde into acetate, and variants can alter metabolism leading to prolonged acetaldehyde levels and physiological flushing responses.
what_would_change_status: A mechanistic review materially revises the ADH1B/ALDH2 role or shows the phenotype description is inaccurate.

claims.claim: The older candidate-gene review singled out ADH1B and ALDH2 as having definitively established contributions to alcohol dependence while describing several other candidate genes as mixed, weak, or controversial; the control therefore calibrates, rather than refutes, candidate-gene skepticism.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass review shows this 2003 conclusion is outdated or inadequate as a control role.

type_payload.fit_rationale: Mechanistically tight enzyme genes, observable intermediate phenotype, and population-specific signal; useful contrast against diffuse psychiatric candidate-gene literatures.
limits: Alcohol flushing GWAS scope is East-Asian-ancestry males in the cited source.
Alcohol dependence and alcohol flushing are related but not identical phenotypes.
Social/cultural drinking context and health harms cannot be collapsed into genotype.

handling_notes: Genetic findings must not be represented as deterministic individual destiny.
No clinical advice, testing advice, or individual-level participant data is encoded.
Population/ancestry, phenotype, and actionability scope must remain visible.

unknowns: Whether to split alcohol flushing and alcohol dependence into separate control records.
How to model culture/environment interactions without genetic determinism.
next_actions: Add a current alcohol-use-disorder genetics review with page locators.
Add an ancestry/phenotype caveat record before pattern synthesis.

scope_qualifiers.ancestry_or_population_scope: East Asian and enzyme-pathway scope emphasized
scope_qualifiers.portability_caution: culture, environment, and drinking behavior not collapsed into genotype
